niche: a regional public health service's wastewater surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 at 24 treatment plants, whose verification desk checks every high-level alert episode on the dashboard: how many episodes last winter's samples raise once the dashboard reads each sample on the shed load (the RNA the sewer destroyed on the way to the plant restored), the basis it moves to on 1 May 2028
answer: Plan the verification desk for 26 alert episodes this winter: last winter's samples raise 26 on the shed load against the 30 the dashboard published (Ardenmouth South, Ardenmouth East, Tarnbrook, Cleaveland Flat and Saltmarsh Point one fewer each, Ardenmouth West one more).
stakeholder_role: the wastewater surveillance coordinator who rosters the verification desk

spine.file: phl_wastewater_results_2026-01_2028-04.csv: the Public Health Laboratory's results export for the 24 plants, one row per sample, target and analysis run, January 2026 to April 2028 (with the 475,268-row inlet historian beside it)
spine.entity: one composite sample, target and analysis run (SARS-CoV-2 N1 or PMMoV, gene copies per litre)
spine.grain: site x sample x target x analysis

world.geography: New Zealand, a fictional region (the public health service, its plants, towns and people are fictional; the decay of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in sewers is modelled on published wastewater studies)

driver: The decisive quantity is each unit's level against its own baseline, read from a measurement that loses part of what it carries in transit at a rate that rises with a covariate moving over the year, so any correction constant over the year cancels against the baseline and leaves every level as recorded, a covariate term added beside the transit length corrects the short transits as much as the long, and only the loss rate as a function of the covariate multiplied by each unit's transit length, recovered from paired measurements at both ends of the transit, moves the levels.
driver_concrete: Each plant's winter 2027 alert episodes on the shed load need the sewer's RNA decay rate as a function of the wastewater's temperature, fitted to the paired upstream study and applied over each plant's population-weighted travel time: a correction constant over the year (the study's average loss, or one rate over each travel time) cancels against each plant's own baseline and leaves the episodes as published, PMMoV normalization leaves the target's own decay in, and a temperature term beside travel time corrects the short sewers as much as the long, while the winter samples at the long trunk sewers lost far less RNA than the summer samples that set their baselines.
stump: A competent solver restores each sample's shed load with the paired study's single decay rate over the plant's travel time (or reads the levels on PMMoV-normalized concentrations) and files the dashboard's published count of winter 2027 alert episodes, because a correction constant over the year cancels against each plant's own baseline; the RNA's decay rate rises with the water's temperature, so the winter samples at the long trunk sewers lost far less than the summer samples that set their baselines, and only the temperature-dependent rate applied over each travel time removes the episodes the colder water alone raised.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads the methods note and the paired study correctly fits one decay rate to the study's ratios of plant to upstream concentration against travel time, restores every sample's shed load with it, recomputes the baselines and levels and files the published episode count, because a rate that does not move over the year scales a plant's winter samples and its baseline alike.
domain_test: The quantity that decides is each plant's level on the shed load, which wastewater-based epidemiology recovers by treating the RNA's decay in the sewer as first order over the population-weighted travel time at a rate that rises with the water's temperature; with another field's nouns there is no sewer travel time, no temperature-driven decay of a virus's RNA and no faecal marker that survives the trip, so the task stops making sense.

differentiation.task133: there a filed outcome curve is conditioned on each unit's own survival to date (a division by survival in a credit book); here a measurement loses part of what it carries in transit at a rate that moves with the season, read against each unit's own baseline, so the only correction that moves anything is the season-dependent part of the loss over each unit's transit length, recovered from paired measurements at both ends
